question: Describe the concept of object-oriented programming (OOP) in Python. What are the four main pillars of OOP?
candidate_answer: Object-oriented programming (OOP) in Python is a programming paradigm that organizes code into "objects," which are instances of classes. A class defines the blueprint for an object, including its attributes (data) and methods (functions that operate on the data). OOP encourages modularity and reusability, allowing you to model real-world entities more effectively. Key concepts include encapsulation (bundling data and methods), inheritance (creating new classes from existing ones), and polymorphism (using methods in different ways across classes).
